Testing statistical significance of random effect

Source: R/pglmm-utils.R
pglmm-profile-LRT.Rd

pglmm_profile_LRT tests statistical significance of the phylogenetic random effect using profile likelihoods when bayes = F.

Usage

pglmm_profile_LRT(x, re.number = 0, cpp = TRUE)

communityPGLMM.profile.LRT(x, re.number = 0, cpp = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A fitted model with class communityPGLMM with bayes = FALSE.

re.number

Which random term to test: positions in x$ss (the standard deviations of the random terms, in the order of the fit). Can be a vector with length >1.

cpp

Whether to use C++ function for optim. Default is TRUE. Only used by the dense code (sparse = FALSE, which is the default only for models that the sparse code does not support, see sparse); ignored if bayes = TRUE, sparse = TRUE or method = "Laplace" (and thus for family = "nbinomial" and "Gamma"): these models are fitted with R code, with the sparse Cholesky factorizations of the Matrix package (CHOLMOD).

Value

A list of likelihood, df, and p-value.

Details

For models fitted with sparse = TRUE (gaussian) or method = "Laplace", it is a likelihood ratio test: the variances of the terms re.number are set to zero and the other parameters are estimated again (as for the profile likelihood intervals of confint.communityPGLMM()). For the other models, the p-values are conditional on the estimates of the other parameters (which are not estimated again), in contrast to a standard likelihood ratio test. As a variance of zero is at the boundary of its range, the p-value of the chi-square test is halved.

For binomial and poisson models fitted with method = "Laplace", the log-likelihoods are the Laplace approximations of the (restricted) marginal log-likelihood (for REML = FALSE, with the fixed effects at their estimates; for REML = TRUE, integrated out).
